## Skillerr 0.1.5

**Trails: your journeys on the web, and a clean start every time**
- Skillerr learns your journeys from how you browse. The pages you open for one thing, in one sitting, become a trail
  like "Kyoto ryokan near Gion", from what they were opened from, what you searched and what they're about.
- Your tabs are left alone while you work: nothing is tucked, grouped or moved.
- When you quit, the tabs still open wait in their trails. Every launch starts with one clean tab, and each waiting
  journey sits between reload and the address bar with its tabs' icons and how far through it you are. Click one for
  its tabs; **Continue** brings them back up, scrolled to where you were.
- A page you closed is done with: it never comes back with its trail.
- Trails notice what you left unfinished: a form you typed into but never sent, an article you read partway, a cart you
  didn't check out, a long video you stopped halfway.
- ⋮ → **Trails**: rename, merge, mark done, forget, never learn from a site, and bring your open Chrome tabs over.
  Prefer your tabs back at launch? Turn off **Start with a clean tab strip**.
- AI apps can see your trails (`my_trails`, `continue_trail`) only after you allow each one once.
- Everything stays on your computer. Trails never keep page text or what you typed. Turn them off in Settings.

**Skillerr Orb: Skillerr's own small AI**
- Built in: one 8 MB file, fast enough to read every page title as you browse. Runs on your CPU, no GPU needed, works
  offline, and nothing leaves your computer.
- It decides which pages belong to one journey, and how far through each you are.
- **Suggests skills from what you keep doing.** When you (or your AIs) do the same kind of task again and again, like
  choosing what to buy with the same searches and review sites, the Orb offers to save how you do it as a skill any AI
  can use. It's worked out from your trails; no AI model writes it.
- **Ask the Orb** on the Trails page finds a trail by what you mean ("plane tickets to Japan" finds your Tokyo flights),
  and the start page says where you were and what you didn't finish.
- **Find anything by meaning** from the address bar: type what you remember, and open, waiting and visited pages
  appear. Enter brings one back where you were.
- **It learns your words, and your AIs'** every week, on your computer, in under a second, and keeps what it learned
  only if it files your pages better. Choose when, and whether it learns from your browsing, your AIs' research or
  both, in Trails settings.
- **Research your AI does** (Claude Desktop, Cursor…) becomes its own trail, named after what it was researching, that
  you can continue later.
- Recall by meaning now works out of the box, without Ollama.

**The Skillerr Orb page**
- ⇧⌘Y opens a map of everything you and your AI apps looked into, with the Orb glowing at the centre and your history
  coming out of it as threads of light: yours in warm colours, your AIs' in cool ones, pages you both opened in green.
  It burns brighter as your history grows. Filter to yours or your AIs', or search by meaning.
- Click the Orb to see what it's doing on your computer: its size, the memory it uses, how fast it is, what it has
  learned, the skills it suggests, and a live log of what it just did.

**History and clearing it**
- ⌘Y opens **History**: every page you and your AIs opened, by day, with search and delete. Pages an AI opened say
  which app.
- **Clear browsing data** (⇧⌘⌫) by time range, from the last hour to all time: browsing history, cookies and site data,
  cached files, research memory, trails, bookmarks.

**Also**
- The live view inside your AI app's chat shows the Skillerr wheel, spinning while your AI drives, and sharper tab
  thumbnails that no longer cut off the page's edges.
- Fixed: an AI's `fetch_page` could read a blank page instead of the one it asked for.

**Install:** `curl -fsSL https://skillerr.com/install.sh | sh` (macOS, Linux) or `irm https://skillerr.com/install.ps1 | iex`
(Windows). Installed copies on Windows, the Linux AppImage and signed Mac builds update themselves.
